22 May
On this day in 1710

Baba Gurbakhash Singh (Banda Bahadur) killed Wajir Khan in Chapud-Chidhi and destroyed Sirhind

Then he established his capital at Mukhlas. Until 1720 everything was conducted from this capital.

22 May brings together four moments of Sikh history, from 1606 to 1964. The main event of the day is from 1710: Baba Gurbakhash Singh (Banda Bahadur) killed Wajir Khan in Chapud-Chidhi and destroyed Sirhind. Together they span three periods, from Miri-Piri and the middle Gurus (1606–1674) to The Punjabi Suba movement (1948–1966). People, places and movements connected with this day include Baba Banda Singh Bahadur, Sirhind (Fatehgarh Sahib), Guru Arjan Dev Ji and the Punjabi Suba movement.

  • 1960Punjabi Suba Convention was held at Amritsar It was attended by Dr. Kitchlew, K.G. Jodh, Zaheer Qurashi and leaders of Socialist and Swatantra Parties.
  • 196411 Sikhs were gunned down at Paonta Sahib (Himachal Pradesh) by the Mahant’s henchmen

Historical background

Miri-Piri and the middle Gurus (1606–1674)

After the martyrdom of Guru Arjan Dev Ji in 1606, Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji wore two swords of miri and piri (temporal and spiritual authority), established the Akal Takht and fought several engagements with Mughal forces. The seventh and eighth Gurus, Guru Har Rai Ji and Guru Har Krishan Ji, led the community from Kiratpur and Delhi, and Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji founded Anandpur (Chak Nanaki) in 1665.

On this day in this period: 1606 The Mughals apprehended Guru Arjan Dev Ji under the Royal decree announced on May 20, 1606.

Banda Singh Bahadur (1709–1716)

Sent north by Guru Gobind Singh Ji, Banda Singh Bahadur led a Sikh uprising that captured Samana and, in 1710, Sirhind, ending the rule of Wazir Khan. He set up Sikh rule from Mukhlisgarh (Lohgarh), issued coins in the name of the Gurus and abolished the zamindari system in the areas he held, before being besieged at Gurdas Nangal and executed in Delhi in 1716.

On this day in this period: 1710 Baba Gurbakhash Singh (Banda Bahadur) killed Wajir Khan in Chapud-Chidhi and destroyed….

The Punjabi Suba movement (1948–1966)

In independent India the Akali Dal campaigned for a Punjabi-speaking state, the Punjabi Suba, through repeated morchas led by Master Tara Singh and Sant Fateh Singh. The demand was met with the reorganisation of Punjab on 1 November 1966, which created present-day Punjab, Haryana and transferred hill areas to Himachal Pradesh.

On this day in this period: 1960 Punjabi Suba Convention was held at Amritsar; 1964 11 Sikhs were gunned down at Paonta Sahib (Himachal Pradesh) by the Mahant’s henchmen.

People and places of this day

Baba Banda Singh Bahadur

The general (1670–1716) sent to Punjab by Guru Gobind Singh Ji. He captured Sirhind in 1710, set up the first Sikh rule with its capital at Lohgarh and ended the zamindari system in the lands he held, before being captured at Gurdas Nangal and executed in Delhi in 1716.

Read more → · Mentioned on 30 other days of the year

Sirhind (Fatehgarh Sahib)

The Mughal provincial town where the younger Sahibzade were executed in December 1704; Gurdwara Fatehgarh Sahib marks the site. Banda Singh Bahadur captured Sirhind in 1710, and the Dal Khalsa took and razed it in 1764.

Read more → · Mentioned on 23 other days of the year

Guru Arjan Dev Ji

The fifth Guru (1563–1606), who built Sri Harmandir Sahib, founded Tarn Taran and Kartarpur (Jalandhar), and compiled the Adi Granth in 1604. He was tortured to death in Lahore in 1606, the first Sikh martyr Guru.

Read more → · Mentioned on 12 other days of the year

The Punjabi Suba movement

The campaign of 1947–1966 for a Punjabi-speaking state, led by the Akali Dal under Master Tara Singh and Sant Fateh Singh, with mass morchas in 1955 and 1960–61. It succeeded when Punjab was reorganised on 1 November 1966; Darshan Singh Pheruman died on a fast in 1969 over the transfer of Chandigarh.

Mentioned on 27 other days of the year

Amritsar

The city founded by Guru Ram Das Ji around the sacred pool of Amritsar. As the home of Sri Harmandir Sahib and the Akal Takht it has been the spiritual and political centre of the Sikhs for four centuries.
